PyTorch explicitly warns that mathematically identical batched and singleton computations need not be bitwise identical: kernels and reduction order can differ. Packed GRU versus unpadded singleton discrepancies therefore do not automatically indicate padding leakage. Compare identical weights in `eval()` under `no_grad()`, with autocast disabled; record device, dtype, PyTorch/CUDA/cuDNN versions and precision settings. Repeat with TF32 disabled using version-supported controls, then FP64 as a diagnostic reference. Determinism controls reproducibility, not equality across different computation paths. [Numerical accuracy](https://docs.pytorch.org/docs/main/notes/numerical_accuracy.html), [CUDA precision controls](https://docs.pytorch.org/docs/main/notes/cuda.html).

Recommended isolation protocol: construct several left-padded representations of the same history. For packing, first compact valid tokens into chronological prefixes and supply their lengths; never pack left-padded tensors directly. Build an explicit recurrent reference using the trained GRU weights, preserving hidden states at padding positions with `where(valid, proposed_state, previous_state)` at every layer. Match PyTorch’s reset/update/new gate order and its reset-after-hidden-projection candidate equation, including biases. Compare every aligned valid-token state against unpadded singleton and packed execution; read the final nonpadding position, never `count-1` in left-padded coordinates. Zero input embeddings alone do not guarantee unchanged recurrent states. [GRU equations](https://docs.pytorch.org/docs/main/generated/torch.nn.GRU.html).

Use explicit, predeclared tolerances: `abs(actual-reference) <= atol + rtol*abs(reference)`. Report maximum absolute error, normalized tolerance violations, and the first divergent token; absolute tolerance matters near zero. PyTorch’s FP32 `assert_close` defaults are `rtol=1.3e-6`, `atol=1e-5`, not universal GRU guarantees. Also compare identical candidate-score vectors, top-10 membership and boundary margins. Analytically, score errors bounded by ε preserve pair ordering when the reference gap exceeds 2ε; near-tie swaps alone are weak evidence of padding bugs. [Comparison semantics](https://docs.pytorch.org/docs/stable/testing).
